test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 3 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What was the main reason for calling off the Non-Cooperation Movement by Gandhiji in 1922?

options.text: Gandhiji was arrested and compelled to stop the movement
A police station at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh was set on fire by a mob
The movement was completed by achieving the target

solution:
The correct answer is **__A police station at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh was set on fire by a mob.__**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The non-cooperation movement was launched in 1920** with the aim of obtaining self-governance and ultimately getting the British colonial authorities to grant full independence to India
 
• The Non-Cooperation Movement was called off by **Gandhiji after the incident of Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh**. 
 
• On 5th Feb of 1922, the protest became violent when protesting people set fire a police station, burning 22 policemen alive

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **After an angry mob murdered police officers in the village of Chauri Chaura (now in Uttar Pradesh state) in February 1922, Gandhi himself called off the movement**; the next month he was arrested without incident.
 
• The movement marked the transition of Indian nationalism from a middle-class to a mass basis
